pr_body:
fixes #5328 

This PR adds better support for casting from string to integers (including `HUGEINT`) when exponents and/or decimals are involved.

Examples:
`'1.234e3'::INTEGER` was previously evaluated to `1000` and is now evaluated to `1234`.
`'125e-1'::INTEGER` was previously evaluated to `12` and is now evaluated to `13`.
`'150e-1'::TINYINT` was previously considered a Conversion Error and is now evaluated to `15`.
pr_comments:
I tried
```sql
select '0.000005'::INTEGER
```
Which gave me `1`
I'm not sure that's correct?

```sql
select '1.1000004'::INTEGER;
```
becomes `2` ?

Could you fix these problems and add additional tests for it?

Out of these rounding modes, which one does DuckDB follow?
```
rounding ['TIE_TO_EVEN', 'TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO', 'TRUNCATE', 'CEILING', 'FLOOR']
```
I think `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` right?
That seems to be the current behavior, and what I've seen from reviewing this code, decimal `>= 5` is how we determine if we should round up.

This seems to be the source for that table btw, it came from Substrait but I did some digging:
<https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/numbers/rounding-modes.html>

On `main` this is the current behavior:
```sql
D select '-0.5'::INTEGER;
┌─────────────────────────┐
│ CAST('-0.5' AS INTEGER) │
│          int32          │
├─────────────────────────┤
│                      -1 │
└─────────────────────────┘
D select '0.5'::INTEGER;
┌────────────────────────┐
│ CAST('0.5' AS INTEGER) │
│         int32          │
├────────────────────────┤
│                      1 │
└────────────────────────┘
```

Which sounds like it corresponds to `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` (or `Half Up` in the linked page)

> Out of these rounding modes, which one does DuckDB follow?

@Tishj  `TIE_AWAY_FROM_ZERO` is indeed the intended behaviour.

issue_context.title: String to HUGEINT cast bug
issue_context.body:
### What happens?

Casting from string to hugeint behaves incorrect.

### To Reproduce

```sql
D  select '1.8259857912588366e+37'::hugeint;
┌───────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CAST('1.8259857912588366e+37' AS HUGEINT) │
│                  int128                   │
├───────────────────────────────────────────┤
│    20000000000000000000000000000000000000 │
└───────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
But this works.
```sql
D select 1.8259857912588366e+37::hugeint;
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CAST(1.8259857912588366e+37 AS HUGEINT) │
│                 int128                  │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  18259857912588365870837119913054699520 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### OS:

iOS

### DuckDB Version:

master

### DuckDB Client:

CLI

### Full Name:

Tania Bogatsch

### Affiliation:

DuckDB Labs

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

### Have you tried the steps to reproduce? Do they include all relevant data and configuration? Does the issue you report still appear there?

- [X] I agree
comments:
Seems to be caused on the first run of `HugeIntegerCastOperation::HandleExponent` (`cast_operators.cpp:1518`)
where before `Flush()` is called the data is:
```
(lldb) p result
(duckdb::HugeIntCastData) $30 = {
  hugeint = (lower = 1, upper = 0)
  intermediate = 1
  digits = '\0'
  decimal = true
}
```
and after:
```
(lldb) p result
(duckdb::HugeIntCastData) $31 = {
  hugeint = (lower = 2, upper = 0)
  intermediate = 0
  digits = '\0'
  decimal = true
}
```
Note: this is not me assigning myself, just got curious and thought I'd share some seemingly useful findings ;)

I tested it with `INT` and got similar result.

```sh
duckdb> select '1.8259857912588366e4'::int;
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ CAST('1.8259857912588366e4' AS INTEGER) │
╞═════════════════════════════════════════╡
│                                   20000 │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

So I think the cause is that `HugeIntegerCastOperation::HandleDecimal` and `IntegerCastOperation::HandleDecimal` called in `IntegerCastLoop` round the decimal even when there is an exponent.

https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/0f0461113f3341135471805c9928c4d71d1f5874/src/common/operator/cast_operators.cpp#L884-L892
`IntegerCastLoop` calls generic `HandleDecimal` here.

If no one has started on it, I will try fixing it later.
Hmm that sounds likely, DECIMAL had a similar issue, maybe have a look at how it's handled there - or if you can come up with a nicer solution, that's even better :)

I looked at `DecimalCastOperation`, and it seems to handle the fractional part better than `IntegerCastOperation` and `HugeIntegerCastOperation`.
`DecimalCastOperation` stores the integer and decimal part in one value first.

https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/0f0461113f3341135471805c9928c4d71d1f5874/src/common/operator/cast_operators.cpp#L1594-L1617

https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/0f0461113f3341135471805c9928c4d71d1f5874/src/common/operator/cast_operators.cpp#L1677-L1697

`DecimalCastOperation::HandleDigit` stores the integer part in `state.result`, and `DecimalCastOperation::HandleDecimal` stores the fractional part in `state.result` too.

Later it adjusts scale and decides whether to round up or down if needed.

Maybe this logic can be reused in `IntegerCastOperation` and `HugeIntegerCastOperation`.
